main_text.p: tiæ & delitiæ. 4. Efd.[?] 7. Vbi enim sunt gau-dia? (canit ecclesia) nirgend mehr dann da/ da die engel singen noua cantica: vnd die schellen Klingen in regis curia: Ia[?] wern wir da/ &c.

Secundò oftendit hoc prouerbium, re de-trimentosam esse stultitiam. Nam vesanus homo, inquit, abligurit, seu deuorat illum. i. thesaurum à maioribus haereditate relictû, hoc est, vt sapiens diuitias parit, sic stultus eas decoquit. Hinc supra Prouer. 14. Sapiens mulier domum suam instruit: stulta suis manibus euertit. Deus sapientiæ liberet nos à stultitia, & det nobis spiritum sapientiæ, vt possimus cum filio eius & sponso pulcherrimo intrare ad nuptias illas cœleftes, Amen.
main_text.head: CONCIO XXIX.
Hoseæ 4.

p.i: Ornicatio & vinum atq; mu-stum auferunt cor. Populus meus lignum suum consul-tat, & baculus eius nunciat ei. Quia spiritus fornicationum fecit(e-um) errare, & fortati sunt à Deo suo.

main_text.p: 1 Duo sunt mala potissimum, quæ clade afficiunt matrimonium, fornicatio & ebrietas: quia vinculum matrimonij frangunt, & egestatem coniugibus inferunt, Matt. 5. Ec-cles. 19. Ideo toties scripturæ sanctæ ab his

page.notes: Running head and page number read as printed; the page number "182" is slightly blurred. Woodcut initial at the start of the epigraph is an ornamental O (the letter is joined to "Ornicatio"); the O is partly hidden, so the initial letter is uncertain. "Efd." is printed this way; the abbreviation may be Esd. or Eccl., so it is marked [?]. "Ia" in the black-letter line is uncertain. Black-letter German passages are marked with bl. The catchword "vitiis" stands alone at the right below the last line. Hyphenated line-end words: "gau-dia", "de-trimentosam", "mu-stum", "consul-tat", "fecit(e-um)", "Ec-cles.".
